Der Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverband ist die Stimme der Verbraucher:innen – und damit eine entscheidende Kraft in der Politik. Wir wissen, was Verbraucher:innen bewegt und verschaffen ihnen Gehör bei Politik, Wirtschaft und Verwaltung. Dazu zählen Publikationen, Social-Media-Grafiken, Flyer, Visuals für Veranstaltungen und Kampagnen sowie digi- tale Formate. Im Juli 2025 wurde die neue Marke Verbraucherzentrale mit einem überarbeiteten Corporate Design eingeführt. Grundlage hierfür ist die strategische Positionierung der Marke Verbraucherzentrale. Article premier : Objet et étendue de la consultation 1.1 - Objet de la consultation Le CROUS de Montpellier assure des services d’hébergement et de restauration pour les étudiants de l’académie de Montpellier. April 2022 nicht an Personen oder Unternehmen vergeben werden, die einen Bezug zu Russland im Sinne der Vorschrift aufweisen. Dies umfasst sowohl unmittelbar als Bewerber, Bieter oder Auftragnehmer auftretende Personen oder Unternehmen als auch mittelbar, mit mehr als zehn Prozent, gemessen am Auftragswert, beteiligte Unterauftragnehmer, Lieferanten oder Eignungsverleiher. Ein Bezug zu Russland im Sinne der Vorschrift besteht durch die russische Staatsangehörigkeit des Bewerbers/Bieters oder die Niederlassung des Bewerbers/Bieters in Russland, durch die Beteiligung einer natürlichen Person oder eines Unternehmens, auf die eines der Kriterien nach Buchstabe a zutrifft, am Bewerber/Bieter über das Halten von Anteilen im Umfang von mehr als 50 Prozent, durch das Handeln der Bewerber/Bieter im Namen oder auf Anweisung von Personen oder Unternehmen, auf die die Kriterien der Buchstaben a und/oder b zutreffen. Bereits vor dem 9. April 2022 geschlossene Verträge mit solchen Personen oder Unternehmen mit Bezug zu Russland dürfen nur bis zum 10. Oktober 2022 fortgeführt werden. US-Hyperscaler sind als primäre Hosting-Plattform ausge- schlossen. Für die Verarbeitung von Sozialdaten gemäß SGB V ist besondere Sorgfalt anzu- wenden (§§ 67 ff. SGB X). Alle eingesetzten Drittdienste sind auf EU-konformes Hosting zu prüfen. Bei Nutzung von Cloud-Diensten sind zusätzlich die gesetzlichen Vorgaben nach § 393 SGB V zur Verarbeitung von Sozial- und Gesundheitsdaten in der Cloud zu erfüllen. Hierzu zählen insbesondere ein zulässiger Verarbeitungsstandort, die Niederlassung der datenverarbeiten- den Stelle in Deutschland sowie ein aktuelles C5-Typ-2-Testat gemäß § 393 SGB V oder die Vorlage eines Maßnahmenplanes inkl. Meilensteinplanung, der vorsieht innerhalb von 24 Monaten ab Erstellung des Maßnahmenplanes ein C5-Typ2-Testat zu erhalten. Sofern Cloud-Dienste zum Einsatz kommen, sind diese Vorgaben vom Hosting-Anbieter (auch als Unterauftragnehmer) ebenfalls zu erfüllen und nachzuweisen. Der für die Leistung relevante Scope des Testats ist einzubeziehen und nachzuweisen. As a strong, diversified, vertically integrated utility, ESB operates right across the electricity market: from generation, through transmission and distribution, to supply. deliverables_scope.text: ESS MODELS Instantly processing data, manufacturers can optimise manufacturing processes and respond faster to changing customer needs – and this ability reconfigures the entire ecosystem. PRODUCT PERSONALISATION AND SERVITISATION The ability to create more product variants while using the same resources is crucial to building a competitive advantage. That’s why increasing production flexibility has long been a pressing matter for manufacturers. Again, data is the game-changer here. Processing real-time information at all stages of user interactions enables creating product simulations that can be adapted to match unique, individual requirements of the customer. Similarly, many manufacturing businesses now expand the value for their clients by shifting from selling products to selling Product-Service Systems (PSS). Pioneered in the 1960s by Rolls Royce, servitisation relieves customers of capital costs, instead offering them advanced solutions in a subscription model. 16 PLATFORMISATION OF PRODUCTION Just as products are now increasingly offered as a service, the manufacturing process is also subject to similar changes. Digital technologies enable breaking it into specific services that can be bought on-demand by other companies (Manufacturing-as-a-Service). Benefitting from

logistics is giving place to digitised distribution enabled by specialised fulfilment centres – very much like in e-commerce. Of course, boosting processes with technology isn’t new. However, what differentiates Logistics 4.0 are progressive datification and smart automation – both translating into increased agility and faster delivery. REORGANISATION OF COMPANIES Industry 4.0 reconfigures the nature of work both in terms of managing both the process and people. The fourth industrial revolution departs from Lean Manufacturing and favours Agile methodologies. Agile Manufacturing focuses on delivering products that closely match clients’ requirements while controlling costs and quality to ensure a relatively low final price and the fastest possible Time to Market. Intelligent technologies help to achieve this objective, so the need for a highly-skilled workforce is also of paramount importance. 3 Michael Mandel, The Rise of the Internet of Goods, available from: http://www.progressivepolicy.org/wp-content/ uploads/2018/08/Internetofgoods-reportPPI-2018.pdf THE RIGHT COMBINATION OF TECHNOLOGIES AND SKILLED WORKFORCE OPENS A MULTITUDE OF BENEFITS TO MANUFACTURERS Increased efficiency and productivity Intelligent technologies allow producing more at lower costs and with less waste.

As a result, factories can monitor and act upon performance information remotely and in real- time. At the same time, physical automation and robotics can supplement labour capacity. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY The report features conclusions based on 12 structured, in-depth interviews with representatives of the Industry 4.0 sector in Wroclaw. The main goal was to learn more about how they perceive their current situation – on an individual and collective level. 9 Conducted by an external researcher in September 2020, all interviews were kept anonymous to ensure maximum confidentiality, trust, and openness of the participants. CEOs, managing directors, and senior managers who took part in the survey represent the three different types of organisations: • local production sites and Shared Services Centres (SSC) of international manufacturers; • small, medium and large companies implementing IT solutions – working on software, embedded software, and hardware projects; • a foundation promoting the development of Industry 4.0 in Poland. ABOUT THE EXPERTS The conclusions were accompanied by commentaries of leading industry experts: Rafał Pisz (Board Member at ITCorner), Maciej Borkowski (Vice-President of The Association of Business Service Leaders – ABSL, Head of Wroclaw Chapter), Andrzej Soldaty (expert in industrial automation, business leader, and President of the Future Industry Platform Foundation), Prof. E

of the Future Industry Platform Foundation), Prof. Edward Chlebus (Head of the CAMT Centre of Excellence at the Wroclaw University of Science and T echnology), Piotr Beling (member of SODA – Software Development Association Poland), and Dr Magdalena Okulowska (President of the Wroclaw Agglomeration Development Agency – ARAW). The study was created by ARAW with the help of partners. 10 ABOUT THE STUDY PARTNERS SDZLEGAL SCHINDHELM is a member of the international SCHINDHELM network of law and tax firms serving business clients in 29 locations in 14 countries. ON INDUSTRY 4.0 WORLDWIDE Before the outbreak of COVID-19, there was widespread interest in Industry 4.0. The sector’s value was projected to grow up to $3.7 trillion by 20259. However, despite these positive outlooks, the actual landscape of Industry 4.0 adoption has been far more complex. ASPIRATIONS VS REALITY 90% of respondents in McKinsey’s10 annual survey admitted seeing the benefits of digital transformation in manufacturing. A majority of them included introducing new technologies as an essential part of their organisational development strategies. However, as research from the World Economic Forum11 demonstrates, despite these declarations, the reality was still far from this ideal. In 2018, the adoption of technology in production still remained slow across industries and regions. ip_data_security.text: This change wouldn’t be possible without advancements such as the Internet of Things (IoT), the Cloud, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), or Artificial Intelligence (AI). 13 Therefore, this publication follows the BCG’s definition of Industry 4.01, seeing it as a transformation that enables analysing data across machines and using it for more efficient manufacturing at reduced costs. CORE TECHNOLOGIES SUPPORTING INDUSTRY 4.0 Autonomous robots & cobots Digital Twins & simulation The AI-powered cloud Augmented & virtual reality Digital integration systems The Industrial Internet of Things Additive manufacturing Big Data & analytics Cybersecurity * ORGANISED AFTER THE BOSTON CONSUL TING GROUP Apart from increasing productivity, Industry 4.0 also encourages developing new products and business models. As a result, it modifies the workforce profile and reconfigures the competitiveness of companies and regions. These issues will be discussed later on in this chapter but first, let’s focus on the three core advancements differentiating Industry 4.0 from the previous revolutions. DATIFICATION Integrating data from devices, sensors, and IT systems enables developing new solutions at all stages of the product lifecycle – from design to production, logistics and maintenance. 1

ntinuously collecting, analysing, and using data in real-time. IIoT enables monitoring of all production processes and scheduling maintenance accordingly. When integrating Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Customer Relationship Management (CRM), the network allows for comprehensive management of all related operations. THE CONVERGENCE OF IT SYSTEMS AND OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY (OT) In the past, IT and OT worked as separate entities: the first one mostly serving management, the latter controlling machines and resources. Thanks to the IIoT, these two worlds have been increasingly converging. Cyber-physical systems (CPS) embody this tendency as machines now combine both the IT and operational qualities. One of the most advanced CP systems – Digital Twins – enables creating digital replicas of physical objects but also processes based on data collected from sensors. ROBOTISATION AND AUTOMATION Industry 4.0 is also underpinned by a growing level of robotisation and automation. Apart from automated production lines, factories now boast autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and collaborative robots (cobots). Įgaliotoji organizacija – pirkimams organizuoti, pirkimo procedūroms iki sutarties ar preliminariosios sutarties sudarymo atlikti, taip pat atlikto pirkimo procedūrų ataskaitai ar skelbimui apie sudarytą sutartį ar preliminariąją sutartį pateikti perkančiosios organizacijos įgaliota organizacija, nurodyta specialiosiose pirkimo sąlygose. Komisija – viešojo pirkimo komisija. Perkančioji organizacija – specialiosiose pirkimo sąlygose nurodyta perkančioji organizacija. Pirkimas – perkančiosios organizacijos atliekamas viešasis pirkimas. Preliminarioji sutartis – preliminarioji viešojo pirkimo-pardavimo sutartis (jei taikoma), vienos ar k

PĮ 49 straipsnį (jeigu perkančioji organizacija nustato tiekėjo kvalifikacijos reikalavimus); pasiūlymo teikimo metu žinomi subtiekėjai (jeigu perkančioji organizacija nustato reikalavimus dėl subtiekėjų pašalinimo pagrindų). fiziniai asmenys, kuriuos tiekėjas ketina įdarbinti Pirkimo laimėjimo atveju ir kurių pajėgumais tiekėjas remiasi pagal VPĮ 49 (kvazisubtiekėjai) (jeigu perkančioji organizacija nustato reikalavimus dėl fizinių asmenų, kurių kvalifikacija tiekėjas remiasi ir kuriuos, pirkimo laimėjimo atveju, tiekėjas ketina įdarbinti, pašalinimo pagrindų). EBVPD pildomas jį įkėlus interneto svetainėje http://ebvpd.eviesiejipirkimai.lt/espd-web/. Tiekėjas, pildydamas EBVPD, laukelyje „Procedūros tipas“ turi pasirinkti „Atvira“. Teikdamas pasiūlymą CVP IS priemonėmis šį EBVPD tiekėjas turi pridėti kartu su kitais pasiūlymo dokumentais (pasiūlymo pateikimo skiltyje „Prisegti dokumentus“). EBVPD nurodytą informaciją pagrindžiantys dokumentai kartu su pasiūlymu neteikiami. Perkančioji organizacija bet kuriuo pirkimo procedūros metu gali paprašyti dalyvių pateikti visus ar dalį dokumentų, patvirtinančių jų pašalinimo pagrindų nebuvimą, atitiktį kvalifikacijos reikalavimams ir, jeigu taikytina, kokybės vadybos sistemos ir (arba) aplinkos apsaugos vadybos sistemos standartams, jeig

p> 

  1. The FSM Department of Health & Social Affairs hereby invites you to submit a quotation for the following works:

 

Lot 1: Website Design & Development Services for the Yap Women Association Digital Village

 

Lot 2: Development of a User-Friendly Point of Sale (POS) System for Women-led Businesses in FSM

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

Website Migration Services The successful tenderer shall be responsible for the migration of CORU's existing live website to the proposed hosting environment. The migration service shall include, at a minimum: • Development and execution of a detailed migration plan, including timelines, responsibilities, testing and implementation activities. • Migration of all website content, functionality, configurations and associated assets to the proposed environment. • Measures to minimise disruption to website availability and user experience during the migration process. • Comprehensive testing prior to go -live, including functional, security, performance, accessibility and user acceptance testing. • Provision of rollback and recovery procedures in the event of migration issues. • Preservation of existing search engine rankings and implementation of any necessary redirects and SEO protections during migration. • Post-migration support to address any issues arising following implementation. references_experience.text:
The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Technical Assistance Facility under the Learning Acceleration in Secondary Education (LAISE) Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include undertaking a comprehensive assessment of ICT infrastructure and institutional readiness, the status and readiness of Multimedia Classrooms (MMCs), and teachers’ competencies and readiness to deliver ICT-enabled teaching using ICT facilities and MMCs.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.dshe.gov.bd or can be obtained at the address given below. The duration of the assignment will be about 06 (Six) months. The assignment is expected to commence in March 2027.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest will be assessed based on the follo

staffing_team.text:
igible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest will be assessed based on the following criteria:

  • General Experience of the Firm (core business and years in business).
  • Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required area. Experience in development partner-financed contracts will be considered an advantage.
  • Firm’s in-house staffing resources with relevant expertise (extent of relevant expertise available among the staff who are on the firm’s regular payroll). 
  • Firm’s relevant organizational capabilities for the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated during the assessment of Expressions of Interest.

Consultants are requested to submit but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

(a) The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/Registration documents from the country of the firm; (b) JV agreement/letter of intent (if applicable); (c) Firm’s brochure;

sla_onsite.text:
and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may affect the Consultant’s consideration for the assignment.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 9:00 to 16:00 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 17:00 hours BST on 09 December 2026.

(Professor Md. Asaduzzaman)

Revenue requires a platform for 200 users that provides access to relevant, high -quality learning content on current technologies and industry practices. The platform should have a clear, intuitive catalogue that enables users to easily search for and access relevant learning materia ls. The provider must ensure that content is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect developments in technology and industry practices. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

f_Objectives_-_SOO.pdf ===== STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed

To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers. Kõigi viie rolli täitjad peavad olema pakkumuses nimeliselt esitatud ning nende vastavus vastavale rollile kehtestatud nõuetele peab olema tõendatud pakkumuses esitataval meeskonnaliikmete ühise CV vormil. Üks meeskonnaliige võib täita kuni kahte rolli, kui ta vastab mõlema rolli nõuetele. Meeskonnaliikmete esitamisega kinnitab pakkuja, et esitatud meeskonnaliikmed hakkavad riigihanke tulemusel sõlmitud lepingu alusel töid teostama. Üks meeskonnaliige võib korraga olla kuni kahes rollis, kui ta täidab mõlema kaetava rolli tingimused. Small Businesses that have completed their Phase 1 contract and where the innovation remains of interest to Canada may receive an invitation, by way of a request for documentation, to advance to Phase 2 at the sole discretion of Canada. There is no minimum TRL level for a Phase 1 innovation to advance to Phase 2. Small businesses must still meet the Eligibility Criteria in 1.4 and must provide all documentation outlined in Attachment 3 when requested. A request for documentation does not guarantee that a Phase 2 contract will be awarded. Small businesses should not have any expectations of being invited to advance to Phase 2. 3 Introduction Since 2007 Switzerland and selected EU Member States have been striving to jointly reduce economic and social disparities in Europe. According to the motto ‘do good and make it known’, this manual encourages Switzerland’s partner states to share results an d make them visible. The aim of this manual is to define the responsibilities, strategies and tools to make the general public aware of Switzerland’s cooperation programmes and to ensure transparency as well as consistent communication in the partner states. The manual specifies the requirements related to communication on the Swiss contribution to selected EU Member States. It states the general requirements and best practices related to the development of a communication concept, communication tools and t he provision of meaningful visual material. Five rules for film production Keep it simple Keep the messages as simple as possible, so that the film can be presented in a way that is immediately understandable. Stick to basics as the viewer often knows little about the subject matter. Avoid specialist jargon and abbreviations. Make your film short and catchy Make clear in the first 30 seconds what the film is about and grab the viewer’s attention. The entire film should not be longer than five minutes. Let the viewer dive into the cooperation programme Use the added value of the film medium and show the situation on site. In this respect the Swiss authorities rely on your support as you are on site and closer to the support measures. While good quality amateur photos can be used as illustrations on occasion, experience from the previous Swiss Cooperation Programme has shown that hiring a professional photographer to document Swiss -funded support measures, activities and events is a good investment. It is therefore a requirement that the partner states mandate professional photographers who take pictures at the start, during and after completion of each support measure. A contract must be set up specifying that the rights of use and of exploitation as well as all intellectual property rights, including copyright and their dissemination, are the property of the customer. Ensure that the donor institution also has full rights to use the photo material as often as it wants. Four rules for better pictures Select images showing people in action Select images showing the challenges before the implementation of the support measure, the work being carried out as well as tangible results. sla_onsite.text: ograniczać możliwość wykorzystania podatności. Wykonawca poinformuje Zamawiającego o zastosowanym zabezpieczeniu i jego wpływie na działanie systemu. Wdrożenie zabezpieczenia tymczasowego nie zastępuje obowiązku trwałego usunięcia podatności. Jeżeli trwałe usunięcie podatności zależy od udostępnienia poprawki przez producenta komponentu, zmiana terminu wymaga udokumentowanego uzasadnienia, utrzymania skutecznego zabezpieczenia tymczasowego oraz pisemnej akceptacji Zamawiającego. Usunięcie podatności musi zostać potwierdzone ponowną weryfikacją i udokumentowane. Powyższe terminy obowiązują niezależnie od terminów obsługi awarii określonych w SLA i nie zmieniają warunków odbioru końcowego, w szczególności zakazu występowania podatności Critical i High. Wykonawca przystępuje do realizacji prac wyłącznie na podstawie zlecenia Zamawiającego, o którym mowa w ust. 8. Wykonanie prac objętych danym zleceniem podlega odbiorowi przez Zamawiającego, potwierdzanemu protokołem odbioru. Z chwilą podpisania protokołu odbioru dochodzi do odbioru prac objętych danym zleceniem. Do procedury odbioru stosuje się odpowiednio postanowienia § 3 ust. 2 i 3 umowy. Wykonawca zobowiązany jest do prowadzenia ewidencji wykorzystania roboczogodzin oraz przekazywania Zamawiającemu informacji o stopniu ich wykorz

estów oraz usunięcia stwierdzonych błędów przed odbiorem końcowym. Utrzymanie i wsparcie W okresie utrzymania Wykonawca zobowiązany będzie do: zapewnienia ciągłości działania serwisu internetowego i BIP; aktualizowania systemu CMS, komponentów i bibliotek; monitorowania działania rozwiązania; usuwania awarii i błędów; obsługi podatności bezpieczeństwa zgodnie z terminami i zasadami określonymi w umowie, w tym w zakresie zabezpieczeń tymczasowych, trwałego usuwania podatności, całodobowej obsługi podatności krytycznych i aktywnie wykorzystywanych, dokumentowania i weryfikacji usunięcia podatności oraz warunków zmiany terminów, niezależnie od SLA dotyczącego awarii i warunków odbioru końcowego; wykonywania kopii zapasowych; świadczenia wsparcia technicznego dla Zamawiającego; realizacji drobnych modyfikacji i zmian rozwojowych w ramach określonego pakietu godzin. Szkolenia Wykonawca przeprowadzi szkolenie dla co najmniej 10 pracowników Zamawiającego w zakresie: obsługi systemu CMS, publikacji i edycji treści, zarządzania użytkownikami, podstawowych zasad bezpieczeństwa związanych z eksploatacją systemu. Szkolenie powinno mieć charakter praktyczny i zostać przeprowadzone na wdrożonym systemie lub środowisku testowym odpowiadającym środowisku docelowemu. Szkolenia Wykonawca przeprowadzi szkolenie dla co najmniej 10 pracowników Zamawiającego w zakresie: obsługi systemu CMS, publikacji i edycji treści, zarządzania użytkownikami, podstawowych zasad bezpieczeństwa związanych z eksploatacją systemu. Szkolenie powinno mieć charakter praktyczny i zostać przeprowadzone na wdrożonym systemie lub środowisku testowym odpowiadającym środowisku docelowemu. Utrzymanie i SLA Wymagania ogólne W okresie utrzymania Wykonawca zobowiązany będzie do świadczenia usług wsparcia i utrzymania zapewniających prawidłowe funkcjonowanie systemu. Minimalne parametry SLA Wykonawca zapewni przez cały okres utrzymania: dostępność co najmniej 99,8% w każdym miesiącu kalendarzowym, mierzoną odrębnie dla serwisu WWW, BIP, modułu rejestracji oraz API; czas reakcji na awarię krytyczną — maksymalnie 15 minut; czas przywrócenia prawidłowego działania po awarii krytycznej — maksymalnie 1 godzinę; obsługę awarii krytycznych całodobowo, 7 dni w tygodniu, również w dni wolne od pracy. Za awarię krytyczną uznaje się niedostępność któregokolwiek z wymienionych elementów lub nieprawidłowość uniemożliwiającą realizację jego podstawowych funkcji, w szczególności dostęp do informacji publicznej, dokonanie rejestracji lub korzy

Wykonawca jest obowiązany wykazać w ofercie, że proponowane rozwiązania w równoważnym stopniu spełniają wymagania określone w OPZ. 3.4. Podział zamówienia pomiędzy kilku wykonawców powodowałby konieczność koordynowania wzajemnie powiązanych prac oraz zwiększał ryzyko problemów z integracją, kompatybilnością i odpowiedzialnością za ewentualne nieprawidłowości.
